            'Bathing & Skin Care': 'Bathing | Skin Care',
            'Baby Health': 'Baby Health',

            'Gifting': 'Gifts | Keepsakes',
            'Gift Sets': 'Gifts | Keepsakes',

            'Baby Clothing': 'Baby Clothing',
            'Baby Apparel': 'Baby Clothing',
        },
    }

    for l1, rules in l2_consolidation.items():
        mask = df['unified_level_1'] == l1
        for old_name, new_name in rules.items():
            # Match case-insensitively
            l2_mask = mask & (df['unified_level_2'].str.lower() == old_name.lower())
            df.loc[l2_mask, 'unified_level_2'] = new_name

    return df


# ============================================================
# 7. ENFORCE CONSTRAINTS
# ============================================================

def enforce_subcategory_limits(df):
    """
    Ensure each parent has 3-20 subcategories.
    Merge tiny groups into 'Other' within the parent.
    """
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']

    for depth in range(1, 5):  # Check L2 under L1, L3 under L2, etc.
        parent_col = levels[depth - 1]
        child_col = levels[depth]

        # Build parent keys
        parent_cols = levels[:depth]

        # Group by parent path
        if depth == 1:
            groups = df.groupby(parent_col)
        else:
            groups = df.groupby(parent_cols)

        for parent_key, group in groups:
            children = group[child_col].dropna()
            children = children[children != '']
            unique_children = children.unique()

            if len(unique_children) <= 2 and len(unique_children) > 0:
                # Too few - might be okay, just leave it
                pass

            if len(unique_children) > 20:
                # Too many subcategories - merge the smallest ones
                child_counts = children.value_counts()
                # Keep top 18, merge rest into a combined category
                top_children = set(child_counts.head(18).index)
                mask_parent = (df[parent_cols] == (parent_key if isinstance(parent_key, str) else pd.Series(parent_key, index=parent_cols))).all(axis=1)
                mask_small = mask_parent & (~df[child_col].isin(top_children)) & (df[child_col] != '')
                df.loc[mask_small, child_col] = 'Other Subcategories'

    return df


def check_word_overlap_siblings(df):
    """Check and fix sibling word overlap > 30%."""
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']

    issues = []
    for depth in range(1, 5):
        parent_cols = levels[:depth]
        child_col = levels[depth]

        if depth == 1:
            groups = df.groupby(levels[0])
        else:
            groups = df.groupby(parent_cols)

        for parent_key, group in groups:
            siblings = group[child_col].dropna()
            siblings = sorted(siblings[siblings != ''].unique())

            for i in range(len(siblings)):
                for j in range(i + 1, len(siblings)):
                    overlap = word_overlap_ratio(siblings[i], siblings[j])
                    if overlap > 0.3:
                        issues.append((parent_key, siblings[i], siblings[j], overlap))

    return issues


# ============================================================
# 8. GENERATE OUTPUT
# ============================================================

def generate_hierarchy(df):
    """Generate the hierarchy CSV with all partial paths."""
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']

    all_paths = set()
    for _, row in df.iterrows():
        path = []
        for lvl in levels:
            val = row[lvl]
            if pd.notna(val) and val != '':
                path.append(val)
                padded = tuple(path + [''] * (5 - len(path)))
                all_paths.add(padded)

    result = pd.DataFrame(list(all_paths), columns=levels)
    result = result.sort_values(levels).reset_index(drop=True)
    return result


# ============================================================
# MAIN
# ============================================================

def main():
    print("Loading data...")
    rows = load_data()
    print(f"Loaded {len(rows)} category paths")
    print(f"  Amazon: {sum(1 for r in rows if r['source'] == 'amazon')}")
    print(f"  Facebook: {sum(1 for r in rows if r['source'] == 'facebook')}")
    print(f"  Google: {sum(1 for r in rows if r['source'] == 'google')}")

    print("\nBuilding unified taxonomy...")
    results = build_taxonomy(rows)

    df = pd.DataFrame(results)

    print("\nConsolidating L2 names...")
    df = consolidate_l2_names(df)

    print("\nEnforcing constraints...")
    df = enforce_subcategory_limits(df)

    # Check L1 statistics
    print("\n=== Level 1 Statistics ===")
    l1_counts = df['unified_level_1'].value_counts()
    print(f"Number of L1 categories: {len(l1_counts)}")
    for cat, count in l1_counts.items():
        sources = df[df['unified_level_1'] == cat]['source'].value_counts()
        source_str = ', '.join(f"{s}:{c}" for s, c in sources.items())
        print(f"  {cat}: {count} entries ({source_str})")

    # Check L2 per L1
    print("\n=== Level 2 per Level 1 ===")
    for l1 in sorted(df['unified_level_1'].unique()):
        l2s = df[df['unified_level_1'] == l1]['unified_level_2'].dropna()
        l2s = l2s[l2s != ''].unique()
        print(f"  {l1}: {len(l2s)} L2 subcategories")

    # Check sibling overlap issues
    print("\n=== Sibling Overlap Issues (>30%) ===")
    issues = check_word_overlap_siblings(df)
    if issues:
        for parent, sib1, sib2, overlap in issues[:20]:
            print(f"  Under '{parent}': '{sib1}' vs '{sib2}' = {overlap:.1%}")
    else:
        print("  None found!")

    # Save outputs
    os.makedirs('/root/output', exist_ok=True)

    print("\nSaving unified_taxonomy_full.csv...")
    df.to_csv('/root/output/unified_taxonomy_full.csv', index=False)

    print("Generating hierarchy...")
    hier_df = generate_hierarchy(df)
    print(f"Total unique hierarchy paths: {len(hier_df)}")
    hier_df.to_csv('/root/output/unified_taxonomy_hierarchy.csv', index=False)

    print("\nDone!")
    return df, hier_df


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build a unified 5-level product category taxonomy from Amazon, Facebook,
and Google Shopping category data.

Strategy:
1. Map each source's top-level category to a unified L1 (curated, 10-20 categories)
2. For categories where source L1 maps to a specialized L2 (e.g., "Cell Phones" -> Electronics > Mobile),
   shift the source hierarchy down
3. Apply curated L2 consolidation to merge similar subcategories
4. Standardize names (Title Case, max 5 words, | separator)
5. Validate constraints (sibling overlap, subcategory counts, source distribution)
"""

import csv
import re
import os
from collections import defaultdict, Counter
import pandas as pd

# ============================================================
# 1. LOAD DATA
# ============================================================

def load_data():
    rows = []
    for filepath, source in [
        ('/root/data/amazon_product_categories.csv', 'amazon'),
        ('/root/data/fb_product_categories.csv', 'facebook'),
        ('/root/data/google_shopping_product_categories.csv', 'google'),
    ]:
        enc = 'utf-8-sig' if 'fb_' in filepath else 'utf-8'
        with open(filepath, encoding=enc) as f:
            reader = csv.DictReader(f)
            for row in reader:
                path = row['category_path'].strip().strip('"')
                parts = [p.strip() for p in path.split(' > ')]
                rows.append({'source': source, 'category_path': path, 'parts': parts})
    return rows


# ============================================================
# 2. TEXT STANDARDIZATION
# ============================================================

def to_title_case(name):
    exceptions = {'and', 'or', 'the', 'of', 'for', 'in', 'a', 'an', 'with', 'to', 'by'}
    words = name.split()
    result = []
    for i, w in enumerate(words):
        if w == '&' or w == '|':
            result.append(w)
        elif i == 0 or w.lower() not in exceptions:
            if w.isupper() and len(w) <= 4:
                result.append(w)
            else:
                result.append(w.capitalize())
        else:
            result.append(w.lower())
    return ' '.join(result)


def standardize_name(name):
    name = name.strip()
    name = to_title_case(name)
    # Collapse extra whitespace
    name = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', name)
    return name.strip()


def truncate_to_5_words(name):
    """Ensure at most 5 content words (words excluding | separators)."""
    parts = name.split(' | ')
    all_words = []
    for p in parts:
        all_words.extend(p.split())
    if len(all_words) <= 5:
        return name
    return ' '.join(all_words[:5])


def normalize_for_comparison(name):
    return re.sub(r'[^\w\s]', ' ', name.lower()).strip()


def get_tokens(name):
    stopwords = {'and', 'the', 'of', 'for', 'in', 'a', 'an', 'or', 'with', 'to', 'by', '&'}
    return set(normalize_for_comparison(name).split()) - stopwords


def word_overlap_ratio(name1, name2):
    t1 = get_tokens(name1)
    t2 = get_tokens(name2)
    if not t1 or not t2:
        return 0.0
    return len(t1 & t2) / min(len(t1), len(t2))

def _norm_keys(d):
    """Normalize dictionary keys to lowercase for matching."""
    return {k.lower(): v for k, v in d.items()}


# ============================================================
# 5. ASSIGN UNIFIED LEVELS
# ============================================================

def assign_unified_levels(row, l2_rules):
    """Assign unified taxonomy levels to a single row."""
    parts = row['parts']
    source = row['source']
    unified = ['', '', '', '', '']

    if not parts:
        return unified, 0

    # --- Level 1 ---
    src_l1 = parts[0].strip()
    src_l1_lower = src_l1.lower()
    unified[0] = UNIFIED_L1_MAP.get(src_l1_lower, 'Other')

    # Check if source L1 should shift to become L2
    if src_l1_lower in L1_TO_L2_SHIFT:
        unified[1] = L1_TO_L2_SHIFT[src_l1_lower]
        # Source parts[1:] map to L3, L4, L5
        remaining = parts[1:]
        for i, part in enumerate(remaining[:3]):
            name = standardize_name(part)
            name = truncate_to_5_words(name)
            unified[2 + i] = name
    else:
        # Normal: source parts[1:] map to L2, L3, L4, L5
        remaining = parts[1:]
        for i, part in enumerate(remaining[:4]):
            name = standardize_name(part)
            name = truncate_to_5_words(name)
            unified[1 + i] = name

    # --- Apply L2 consolidation ---
    l1 = unified[0]
    if l1 in l2_rules and unified[1]:
        l2_key = unified[1].lower()
        if l2_key in l2_rules[l1]:
            unified[1] = l2_rules[l1][l2_key]

    # --- Apply L3 consolidation (reuse L2 rules for known sub-patterns) ---
    # Skip - L3+ are already direct mappings from source

    depth = min(len(parts), 5)
    return unified, depth


# ============================================================
# 6. POST-PROCESSING
# ============================================================

def remove_parent_child_overlap(df):
    """Remove word overlap between adjacent levels, but only when overlap is significant."""
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']

    for idx in range(len(df)):
        for i in range(1, 5):
            parent = df.at[idx, levels[i-1]]
            child = df.at[idx, levels[i]]
            if not parent or not child or pd.isna(parent) or pd.isna(child):
                continue

            parent_tokens = get_tokens(parent)
            child_tokens = get_tokens(child)
            if not parent_tokens or not child_tokens:
                continue

            overlap = parent_tokens & child_tokens
            # Only remove if > 50% of child words are in parent
            overlap_ratio = len(overlap) / len(child_tokens)
            if overlap_ratio >= 0.5 and len(child_tokens - overlap) > 0:
                remaining = [w for w in child.split() if w.lower() not in overlap or w in ('&', '|')]
                if remaining:
                    new_name = ' '.join(remaining)
                    new_name = new_name.strip(' |&')
                    if new_name and len(new_name) > 1:
                        df.at[idx, levels[i]] = new_name

    return df


def cap_subcategory_count(df, max_children=20):
    """Merge excess subcategories into 'Other' groups."""
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']

    for depth in range(1, 5):
        parent_cols = levels[:depth]
        child_col = levels[depth]

        for parent_key, group in df.groupby(parent_cols):
            children = group[child_col].dropna()
            children = children[children != '']
            unique_children = children.unique()

            if len(unique_children) > max_children:
                child_counts = children.value_counts()
                keep = set(child_counts.head(max_children - 1).index)

                if isinstance(parent_key, str):
                    mask = (df[parent_cols[0]] == parent_key)
                else:
                    mask = pd.Series(True, index=df.index)
                    for col, val in zip(parent_cols, parent_key):
                        mask &= (df[col] == val)

                merge_mask = mask & (~df[child_col].isin(keep)) & (df[child_col] != '') & df[child_col].notna()
                df.loc[merge_mask, child_col] = 'Other Subcategories'

    return df


def check_sibling_overlap(df):
    """Check word overlap between sibling categories."""
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']
    issues = []

    for depth in range(1, 5):
        parent_cols = levels[:depth]
        child_col = levels[depth]

        for parent_key, group in df.groupby(parent_cols):
            siblings = group[child_col].dropna()
            siblings = sorted(siblings[siblings != ''].unique())

            for i in range(len(siblings)):
                for j in range(i+1, len(siblings)):
                    overlap = word_overlap_ratio(siblings[i], siblings[j])
                    if overlap > 0.3:
                        issues.append((parent_key, child_col, siblings[i], siblings[j], overlap))

    return issues


def verify_source_distribution(df):
    """Check source distribution across L1 categories."""
    print("\n=== Source Distribution per L1 ===")
    for l1 in sorted(df['unified_level_1'].unique()):
        subset = df[df['unified_level_1'] == l1]
        total = len(subset)
        src_counts = subset['source'].value_counts()
        sources_present = set(src_counts.index)
        missing = {'amazon', 'facebook', 'google'} - sources_present
        src_str = ', '.join(f"{s}:{src_counts.get(s,0)}" for s in ['amazon','facebook','google'])
        warning = f" *** MISSING: {missing}" if missing else ""
        print(f"  {l1} ({total}): {src_str}{warning}")


# ============================================================
# 7. GENERATE OUTPUTS
# ============================================================

def generate_hierarchy(df):
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']
    all_paths = set()
    for _, row in df.iterrows():
        path = []
        for lvl in levels:
            val = row[lvl]
            if pd.notna(val) and val != '':
                path.append(val)
                all_paths.add(tuple(path + [''] * (5 - len(path))))
    result = pd.DataFrame(list(all_paths), columns=levels)
    result = result.sort_values(levels).reset_index(drop=True)
    return result


# ============================================================
# MAIN
# ============================================================

def main():
    print("Loading data...")
    rows = load_data()
    print(f"Loaded {len(rows)} rows (amazon:{sum(1 for r in rows if r['source']=='amazon')}, "
          f"facebook:{sum(1 for r in rows if r['source']=='facebook')}, "
          f"google:{sum(1 for r in rows if r['source']=='google')})")

    print("\nBuilding L2 consolidation rules...")
    l2_rules = build_l2_consolidation()

    print("Assigning unified levels...")
    results = []
    for row in rows:
        unified, depth = assign_unified_levels(row, l2_rules)
        results.append({
            'source': row['source'],
            'category_path': row['category_path'],
            'depth': depth,
            'unified_level_1': unified[0],
            'unified_level_2': unified[1],
            'unified_level_3': unified[2],
            'unified_level_4': unified[3],
            'unified_level_5': unified[4],
        })

    df = pd.DataFrame(results)

    print("Capping subcategory counts...")
    df = cap_subcategory_count(df)

    # Stats
    print(f"\n=== Level 1: {df['unified_level_1'].nunique()} categories ===")
    for l1 in sorted(df['unified_level_1'].unique()):
        count = len(df[df['unified_level_1'] == l1])
        l2_count = df[df['unified_level_1'] == l1]['unified_level_2'].dropna()
        l2_count = l2_count[l2_count != ''].nunique()
        print(f"  {l1}: {count} rows, {l2_count} L2 subcategories")

    verify_source_distribution(df)

    # Check overlap
    print("\n=== Sibling Overlap Issues (>30%) at L2 ===")
    issues = check_sibling_overlap(df)
    l2_issues = [i for i in issues if i[1] == 'unified_level_2']
    if l2_issues:
        for parent, level, sib1, sib2, overlap in l2_issues[:30]:
            print(f"  Under '{parent}': '{sib1}' vs '{sib2}' = {overlap:.1%}")
    else:
        print("  None found!")

    # Save
    os.makedirs('/root/output', exist_ok=True)

    print("\nSaving unified_taxonomy_full.csv...")
    df.to_csv('/root/output/unified_taxonomy_full.csv', index=False)

    print("Generating hierarchy...")
    hier_df = generate_hierarchy(df)
    print(f"Total unique hierarchy paths: {len(hier_df)}")
    hier_df.to_csv('/root/output/unified_taxonomy_hierarchy.csv', index=False)

    print("\nDone!")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build a unified 5-level product category taxonomy from Amazon, Facebook,
and Google Shopping category data.

Strategy:
1. Map each source's top-level category to a unified L1 (curated, 10-20 categories)
2. For categories where source L1 maps to a specialized L2 (e.g., "Cell Phones" -> Electronics > Mobile),
   shift the source hierarchy down
3. Apply curated L2 consolidation to merge similar subcategories
4. Standardize names (Title Case, max 5 words, | separator)
5. Validate constraints (sibling overlap, subcategory counts, source distribution)
"""

import csv
import re
import os
from collections import defaultdict, Counter
import pandas as pd

# ============================================================
# 1. LOAD DATA
# ============================================================

def load_data():
    rows = []
    for filepath, source in [
        ('/root/data/amazon_product_categories.csv', 'amazon'),
        ('/root/data/fb_product_categories.csv', 'facebook'),
        ('/root/data/google_shopping_product_categories.csv', 'google'),
    ]:
        enc = 'utf-8-sig' if 'fb_' in filepath else 'utf-8'
        with open(filepath, encoding=enc) as f:
            reader = csv.DictReader(f)
            for row in reader:
                path = row['category_path'].strip().strip('"')
                parts = [p.strip() for p in path.split(' > ')]
                rows.append({'source': source, 'category_path': path, 'parts': parts})
    return rows


# ============================================================
# 2. TEXT STANDARDIZATION
# ============================================================

def to_title_case(name):
    exceptions = {'and', 'or', 'the', 'of', 'for', 'in', 'a', 'an', 'with', 'to', 'by'}
    words = name.split()
    result = []
    for i, w in enumerate(words):
        if w == '&' or w == '|':
            result.append(w)
        elif i == 0 or w.lower() not in exceptions:
            if w.isupper() and len(w) <= 4:
                result.append(w)
            else:
                result.append(w.capitalize())
        else:
            result.append(w.lower())
    return ' '.join(result)


def standardize_name(name):
    name = name.strip()
    name = to_title_case(name)
    # Collapse extra whitespace
    name = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', name)
    return name.strip()


def truncate_to_5_words(name):
    """Ensure at most 5 content words (words excluding | separators)."""
    parts = name.split(' | ')
    all_words = []
    for p in parts:
        all_words.extend(p.split())
    if len(all_words) <= 5:
        return name
    return ' '.join(all_words[:5])


def normalize_for_comparison(name):
    return re.sub(r'[^\w\s]', ' ', name.lower()).strip()


def get_tokens(name):
    stopwords = {'and', 'the', 'of', 'for', 'in', 'a', 'an', 'or', 'with', 'to', 'by', '&'}
    return set(normalize_for_comparison(name).split()) - stopwords

    t1 = get_tokens(name1)
    t2 = get_tokens(name2)
    if not t1 or not t2:

    return len(t1 & t2) / min(len(t1), len(t2))

def _norm_keys(d):
    """Normalize dictionary keys to lowercase for matching."""
    return {k.lower(): v for k, v in d.items()}

# 5. ASSIGN UNIFIED LEVELS
# ============================================================

def assign_unified_levels(row, l2_rules):
    """Assign unified taxonomy levels to a single row."""
    parts = row['parts']
    source = row['source']
    unified = ['', '', '', '', '']

    if not parts:
        return unified, 0

    # --- Level 1 ---
    src_l1 = parts[0].strip()
    src_l1_lower = src_l1.lower()
    unified[0] = UNIFIED_L1_MAP.get(src_l1_lower, 'Other')

    # Check if source L1 should shift to become L2
    if src_l1_lower in L1_TO_L2_SHIFT:
        unified[1] = L1_TO_L2_SHIFT[src_l1_lower]
        # Source parts[1:] map to L3, L4, L5
        remaining = parts[1:]
        for i, part in enumerate(remaining[:3]):
            name = standardize_name(part)
            name = truncate_to_5_words(name)
            unified[2 + i] = name
    else:
        # Normal: source parts[1:] map to L2, L3, L4, L5
        remaining = parts[1:]
        for i, part in enumerate(remaining[:4]):
            name = standardize_name(part)
            name = truncate_to_5_words(name)
            unified[1 + i] = name

    # --- Apply L2 consolidation ---
    l1 = unified[0]
    if l1 in l2_rules and unified[1]:
        l2_key = unified[1].lower()
        if l2_key in l2_rules[l1]:
            unified[1] = l2_rules[l1][l2_key]

    # --- Apply L3 consolidation (reuse L2 rules for known sub-patterns) ---
    # Skip - L3+ are already direct mappings from source

    depth = min(len(parts), 5)
    return unified, depth

def remove_parent_child_overlap(df):
    """Remove word overlap between adjacent levels, but only when overlap is significant."""
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']

    for idx in range(len(df)):
        for i in range(1, 5):
            parent = df.at[idx, levels[i-1]]
            child = df.at[idx, levels[i]]
            if not parent or not child or pd.isna(parent) or pd.isna(child):
                continue

            parent_tokens = get_tokens(parent)
            child_tokens = get_tokens(child)
            if not parent_tokens or not child_tokens:
                continue

            overlap = parent_tokens & child_tokens
            # Only remove if > 50% of child words are in parent
            overlap_ratio = len(overlap) / len(child_tokens)
            if overlap_ratio >= 0.5 and len(child_tokens - overlap) > 0:
                remaining = [w for w in child.split() if w.lower() not in overlap or w in ('&', '|')]
                if remaining:
                    new_name = ' '.join(remaining)
                    new_name = new_name.strip(' |&')
                    if new_name and len(new_name) > 1:
                        df.at[idx, levels[i]] = new_name

    return df


def cap_subcategory_count(df, max_children=20):
    """Merge excess subcategories into 'Other' groups."""
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']

    for depth in range(1, 5):
        parent_cols = levels[:depth]
        child_col = levels[depth]

        for parent_key, group in df.groupby(parent_cols):
            children = group[child_col].dropna()
            children = children[children != '']
            unique_children = children.unique()

            if len(unique_children) > max_children:
                child_counts = children.value_counts()
                keep = set(child_counts.head(max_children - 1).index)

                if isinstance(parent_key, str):
                    mask = (df[parent_cols[0]] == parent_key)
                else:
                    mask = pd.Series(True, index=df.index)
                    for col, val in zip(parent_cols, parent_key):
                        mask &= (df[col] == val)

                merge_mask = mask & (~df[child_col].isin(keep)) & (df[child_col] != '') & df[child_col].notna()
                df.loc[merge_mask, child_col] = 'Other Subcategories'

    return df


def check_sibling_overlap(df):
    """Check word overlap between sibling categories."""
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']
    issues = []

    for depth in range(1, 5):
        parent_cols = levels[:depth]
        child_col = levels[depth]

        for parent_key, group in df.groupby(parent_cols):
            siblings = group[child_col].dropna()
            siblings = sorted(siblings[siblings != ''].unique())

            for i in range(len(siblings)):
                for j in range(i+1, len(siblings)):
                    overlap = word_overlap_ratio(siblings[i], siblings[j])
                    if overlap > 0.3:
                        issues.append((parent_key, child_col, siblings[i], siblings[j], overlap))

    return issues


def verify_source_distribution(df):
    """Check source distribution across L1 categories."""
    print("\n=== Source Distribution per L1 ===")
    for l1 in sorted(df['unified_level_1'].unique()):
        subset = df[df['unified_level_1'] == l1]
        total = len(subset)
        src_counts = subset['source'].value_counts()
        sources_present = set(src_counts.index)
        missing = {'amazon', 'facebook', 'google'} - sources_present
        src_str = ', '.join(f"{s}:{src_counts.get(s,0)}" for s in ['amazon','facebook','google'])
        warning = f" *** MISSING: {missing}" if missing else ""
        print(f"  {l1} ({total}): {src_str}{warning}")

def generate_hierarchy(df):
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']
    all_paths = set()
    for _, row in df.iterrows():
        path = []
        for lvl in levels:
            val = row[lvl]
            if pd.notna(val) and val != '':
                path.append(val)
                all_paths.add(tuple(path + [''] * (5 - len(path))))
    result = pd.DataFrame(list(all_paths), columns=levels)
    result = result.sort_values(levels).reset_index(drop=True)
    return result

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build a unified 5-level product category taxonomy from Amazon, Facebook,
and Google Shopping category data.

Strategy:
1. Map each source's top-level category to a unified L1 (curated, 10-20 categories)
2. For categories where source L1 maps to a specialized L2 (e.g., "Cell Phones" -> Electronics > Mobile),
   shift the source hierarchy down
3. Apply curated L2 consolidation to merge similar subcategories
4. Standardize names (Title Case, max 5 words, | separator)
5. Validate constraints (sibling overlap, subcategory counts, source distribution)
"""

import csv
import re
import os
from collections import defaultdict, Counter
import pandas as pd

# ============================================================
# 1. LOAD DATA
# ============================================================

def load_data():
    rows = []
    for filepath, source in [
        ('/root/data/amazon_product_categories.csv', 'amazon'),
        ('/root/data/fb_product_categories.csv', 'facebook'),
        ('/root/data/google_shopping_product_categories.csv', 'google'),
    ]:
        enc = 'utf-8-sig' if 'fb_' in filepath else 'utf-8'
        with open(filepath, encoding=enc) as f:
            reader = csv.DictReader(f)
            for row in reader:
                path = row['category_path'].strip().strip('"')
                parts = [p.strip() for p in path.split(' > ')]
                rows.append({'source': source, 'category_path': path, 'parts': parts})
    return rows


# ============================================================
# 2. TEXT STANDARDIZATION
# ============================================================

def to_title_case(name):
    exceptions = {'and', 'or', 'the', 'of', 'for', 'in', 'a', 'an', 'with', 'to', 'by'}
    words = name.split()
    result = []
    for i, w in enumerate(words):
        if w == '&' or w == '|':
            result.append(w)
        elif i == 0 or w.lower() not in exceptions:
            if w.isupper() and len(w) <= 4:
                result.append(w)
            else:
                result.append(w.capitalize())
        else:
            result.append(w.lower())
    return ' '.join(result)


def standardize_name(name):
    name = name.strip()
    name = to_title_case(name)
    # Collapse extra whitespace
    name = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', name)
    return name.strip()


def truncate_to_5_words(name):
    """Ensure at most 5 content words (words excluding | separators)."""
    parts = name.split(' | ')
    all_words = []
    for p in parts:
        all_words.extend(p.split())
    if len(all_words) <= 5:
        return name
    return ' '.join(all_words[:5])


def normalize_for_comparison(name):
    return re.sub(r'[^\w\s]', ' ', name.lower()).strip()


def get_tokens(name):
    stopwords = {'and', 'the', 'of', 'for', 'in', 'a', 'an', 'or', 'with', 'to', 'by', '&'}
    return set(normalize_for_comparison(name).split()) - stopwords

    t1 = get_tokens(name1)
    t2 = get_tokens(name2)
    if not t1 or not t2:

    return len(t1 & t2) / min(len(t1), len(t2))

def _norm_keys(d):
    """Normalize dictionary keys to lowercase for matching."""
    return {k.lower(): v for k, v in d.items()}


# ============================================================
# 5. ASSIGN UNIFIED LEVELS
# ============================================================

def assign_unified_levels(row, l2_rules):
    """Assign unified taxonomy levels to a single row."""
    parts = row['parts']
    source = row['source']
    unified = ['', '', '', '', '']

    if not parts:
        return unified, 0

    # --- Level 1 ---
    src_l1 = parts[0].strip()
    src_l1_lower = src_l1.lower()
    unified[0] = UNIFIED_L1_MAP.get(src_l1_lower, 'Other')

    # Check if source L1 should shift to become L2
    if src_l1_lower in L1_TO_L2_SHIFT:
        unified[1] = L1_TO_L2_SHIFT[src_l1_lower]
        # Source parts[1:] map to L3, L4, L5
        remaining = parts[1:]
        for i, part in enumerate(remaining[:3]):
            name = standardize_name(part)
            name = truncate_to_5_words(name)
            unified[2 + i] = name
    else:
        # Normal: source parts[1:] map to L2, L3, L4, L5
        remaining = parts[1:]
        for i, part in enumerate(remaining[:4]):
            name = standardize_name(part)
            name = truncate_to_5_words(name)
            unified[1 + i] = name

    # --- Apply L2 consolidation ---
    l1 = unified[0]
    if l1 in l2_rules and unified[1]:
        l2_key = unified[1].lower()
        if l2_key in l2_rules[l1]:
            unified[1] = l2_rules[l1][l2_key]

    # --- Apply L3 consolidation (reuse L2 rules for known sub-patterns) ---
    # Skip - L3+ are already direct mappings from source

    depth = min(len(parts), 5)
    return unified, depth


# ============================================================
# 6. POST-PROCESSING
# ============================================================

def remove_parent_child_overlap(df):
    """Remove word overlap between adjacent levels, but only when overlap is significant."""
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']

    for idx in range(len(df)):
        for i in range(1, 5):
            parent = df.at[idx, levels[i-1]]
            child = df.at[idx, levels[i]]
            if not parent or not child or pd.isna(parent) or pd.isna(child):
                continue

            parent_tokens = get_tokens(parent)
            child_tokens = get_tokens(child)
            if not parent_tokens or not child_tokens:
                continue

            overlap = parent_tokens & child_tokens
            # Only remove if > 50% of child words are in parent
            overlap_ratio = len(overlap) / len(child_tokens)
            if overlap_ratio >= 0.5 and len(child_tokens - overlap) > 0:
                remaining = [w for w in child.split() if w.lower() not in overlap or w in ('&', '|')]
                if remaining:
                    new_name = ' '.join(remaining)
                    new_name = new_name.strip(' |&')
                    if new_name and len(new_name) > 1:
                        df.at[idx, levels[i]] = new_name

    return df


def cap_subcategory_count(df, max_children=20):
    """Merge excess subcategories into 'Other' groups."""
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']

    for depth in range(1, 5):
        parent_cols = levels[:depth]
        child_col = levels[depth]

        for parent_key, group in df.groupby(parent_cols):
            children = group[child_col].dropna()
            children = children[children != '']
            unique_children = children.unique()

            if len(unique_children) > max_children:
                child_counts = children.value_counts()
                keep = set(child_counts.head(max_children - 1).index)

                if isinstance(parent_key, str):
                    mask = (df[parent_cols[0]] == parent_key)
                else:
                    mask = pd.Series(True, index=df.index)
                    for col, val in zip(parent_cols, parent_key):
                        mask &= (df[col] == val)

                merge_mask = mask & (~df[child_col].isin(keep)) & (df[child_col] != '') & df[child_col].notna()
                df.loc[merge_mask, child_col] = 'Other Subcategories'

    return df


def check_sibling_overlap(df):
    """Check word overlap between sibling categories."""
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']
    issues = []

    for depth in range(1, 5):
        parent_cols = levels[:depth]
        child_col = levels[depth]

        for parent_key, group in df.groupby(parent_cols):
            siblings = group[child_col].dropna()
            siblings = sorted(siblings[siblings != ''].unique())

            for i in range(len(siblings)):
                for j in range(i+1, len(siblings)):
                    overlap = word_overlap_ratio(siblings[i], siblings[j])
                    if overlap > 0.3:
                        issues.append((parent_key, child_col, siblings[i], siblings[j], overlap))

    return issues


def verify_source_distribution(df):
    """Check source distribution across L1 categories."""
    print("\n=== Source Distribution per L1 ===")
    for l1 in sorted(df['unified_level_1'].unique()):
        subset = df[df['unified_level_1'] == l1]
        total = len(subset)
        src_counts = subset['source'].value_counts()
        sources_present = set(src_counts.index)
        missing = {'amazon', 'facebook', 'google'} - sources_present
        src_str = ', '.join(f"{s}:{src_counts.get(s,0)}" for s in ['amazon','facebook','google'])
        warning = f" *** MISSING: {missing}" if missing else ""
        print(f"  {l1} ({total}): {src_str}{warning}")


# ============================================================
# 7. GENERATE OUTPUTS
# ============================================================

def generate_hierarchy(df):
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']
    all_paths = set()
    for _, row in df.iterrows():
        path = []
        for lvl in levels:
            val = row[lvl]
            if pd.notna(val) and val != '':
                path.append(val)
                all_paths.add(tuple(path + [''] * (5 - len(path))))
    result = pd.DataFrame(list(all_paths), columns=levels)
    result = result.sort_values(levels).reset_index(drop=True)
    return result


# ============================================================
# MAIN
# ============================================================

def main():
    print("Loading data...")
    rows = load_data()
    print(f"Loaded {len(rows)} rows (amazon:{sum(1 for r in rows if r['source']=='amazon')}, "
          f"facebook:{sum(1 for r in rows if r['source']=='facebook')}, "
          f"google:{sum(1 for r in rows if r['source']=='google')})")

    print("\nBuilding L2 consolidation rules...")
    l2_rules = build_l2_consolidation()

    print("Assigning unified levels...")
    results = []
    for row in rows:
        unified, depth = assign_unified_levels(row, l2_rules)
        results.append({
            'source': row['source'],
            'category_path': row['category_path'],
            'depth': depth,
            'unified_level_1': unified[0],
            'unified_level_2': unified[1],
            'unified_level_3': unified[2],
            'unified_level_4': unified[3],
            'unified_level_5': unified[4],
        })

    df = pd.DataFrame(results)

    print("Capping subcategory counts...")
    df = cap_subcategory_count(df)

    # Stats
    print(f"\n=== Level 1: {df['unified_level_1'].nunique()} categories ===")
    for l1 in sorted(df['unified_level_1'].unique()):
        count = len(df[df['unified_level_1'] == l1])
        l2_count = df[df['unified_level_1'] == l1]['unified_level_2'].dropna()
        l2_count = l2_count[l2_count != ''].nunique()
        print(f"  {l1}: {count} rows, {l2_count} L2 subcategories")

    verify_source_distribution(df)

    # Check overlap
    print("\n=== Sibling Overlap Issues (>30%) at L2 ===")
    issues = check_sibling_overlap(df)
    l2_issues = [i for i in issues if i[1] == 'unified_level_2']
    if l2_issues:
        for parent, level, sib1, sib2, overlap in l2_issues[:30]:
            print(f"  Under '{parent}': '{sib1}' vs '{sib2}' = {overlap:.1%}")
    else:
        print("  None found!")

    # Save
    os.makedirs('/root/output', exist_ok=True)

    print("\nSaving unified_taxonomy_full.csv...")
    df.to_csv('/root/output/unified_taxonomy_full.csv', index=False)

    print("Generating hierarchy...")
    hier_df = generate_hierarchy(df)
    print(f"Total unique hierarchy paths: {len(hier_df)}")
    hier_df.to_csv('/root/output/unified_taxonomy_hierarchy.csv', index=False)

    print("\nDone!")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build a unified 5-level product category taxonomy from Amazon, Facebook,
and Google Shopping category data.

Strategy:
1. Map each source's top-level category to a unified L1 (curated, 10-20 categories)
2. For categories where source L1 maps to a specialized L2 (e.g., "Cell Phones" -> Electronics > Mobile),
   shift the source hierarchy down
3. Apply curated L2 consolidation to merge similar subcategories
4. Standardize names (Title Case, max 5 words, | separator)
5. Validate constraints (sibling overlap, subcategory counts, source distribution)
"""

import csv
import re
import os
from collections import defaultdict, Counter
import pandas as pd

# ============================================================
# 1. LOAD DATA
# ============================================================

def load_data():
    rows = []
    for filepath, source in [
        ('/root/data/amazon_product_categories.csv', 'amazon'),
        ('/root/data/fb_product_categories.csv', 'facebook'),
        ('/root/data/google_shopping_product_categories.csv', 'google'),
    ]:
        enc = 'utf-8-sig' if 'fb_' in filepath else 'utf-8'
        with open(filepath, encoding=enc) as f:
            reader = csv.DictReader(f)
            for row in reader:
                path = row['category_path'].strip().strip('"')
                parts = [p.strip() for p in path.split(' > ')]
                rows.append({'source': source, 'category_path': path, 'parts': parts})
    return rows


# ============================================================
# 2. TEXT STANDARDIZATION
# ============================================================

def to_title_case(name):
    exceptions = {'and', 'or', 'the', 'of', 'for', 'in', 'a', 'an', 'with', 'to', 'by'}
    words = name.split()
    result = []
    for i, w in enumerate(words):
        if w == '&' or w == '|':
            result.append(w)
        elif i == 0 or w.lower() not in exceptions:
            if w.isupper() and len(w) <= 4:
                result.append(w)
            else:
                result.append(w.capitalize())
        else:
            result.append(w.lower())
    return ' '.join(result)


def standardize_name(name):
    name = name.strip()
    name = to_title_case(name)
    # Collapse extra whitespace
    name = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', name)
    return name.strip()


def truncate_to_5_words(name):
    """Ensure at most 5 content words (words excluding | separators)."""
    parts = name.split(' | ')
    all_words = []
    for p in parts:
        all_words.extend(p.split())
    if len(all_words) <= 5:
        return name
    return ' '.join(all_words[:5])


def normalize_for_comparison(name):
    return re.sub(r'[^\w\s]', ' ', name.lower()).strip()


def get_tokens(name):
    stopwords = {'and', 'the', 'of', 'for', 'in', 'a', 'an', 'or', 'with', 'to', 'by', '&'}
    return set(normalize_for_comparison(name).split()) - stopwords


def word_overlap_ratio(name1, name2):
    t1 = get_tokens(name1)
    t2 = get_tokens(name2)
    if not t1 or not t2:
        return 0.0
    return len(t1 & t2) / min(len(t1), len(t2))

def _norm_keys(d):
    """Normalize dictionary keys to lowercase for matching."""
    return {k.lower(): v for k, v in d.items()}


# ============================================================
# 5. ASSIGN UNIFIED LEVELS
# ============================================================

def assign_unified_levels(row, l2_rules):
    """Assign unified taxonomy levels to a single row."""
    parts = row['parts']
    source = row['source']
    unified = ['', '', '', '', '']

    if not parts:
        return unified, 0

    # --- Level 1 ---
    src_l1 = parts[0].strip()
    src_l1_lower = src_l1.lower()
    unified[0] = UNIFIED_L1_MAP.get(src_l1_lower, 'Other')

    # Check if source L1 should shift to become L2
    if src_l1_lower in L1_TO_L2_SHIFT:
        unified[1] = L1_TO_L2_SHIFT[src_l1_lower]
        # Source parts[1:] map to L3, L4, L5
        remaining = parts[1:]
        for i, part in enumerate(remaining[:3]):
            name = standardize_name(part)
            name = truncate_to_5_words(name)
            unified[2 + i] = name
    else:
        # Normal: source parts[1:] map to L2, L3, L4, L5
        remaining = parts[1:]
        for i, part in enumerate(remaining[:4]):
            name = standardize_name(part)
            name = truncate_to_5_words(name)
            unified[1 + i] = name

    # --- Apply L2 consolidation ---
    l1 = unified[0]
    if l1 in l2_rules and unified[1]:
        l2_key = unified[1].lower()
        if l2_key in l2_rules[l1]:
            unified[1] = l2_rules[l1][l2_key]
        else:
            # Fuzzy fallback: try to match with existing consolidated L2 targets
            best_match = fuzzy_match_l2(l2_key, l2_rules[l1])
            if best_match:
                unified[1] = best_match

    depth = min(len(parts), 5)
    return unified, depth


def fuzzy_match_l2(name, rules_dict):
    """Try to fuzzy match an L2 name to an existing consolidated target."""
    name_tokens = get_tokens(name)
    if not name_tokens:
        return None

    # Get unique target values from rules
    targets = set(rules_dict.values())
    best_target = None
    best_score = 0.0

    for target in targets:
        target_tokens = get_tokens(target)
        if not target_tokens:
            continue
        overlap = len(name_tokens & target_tokens)
        score = overlap / min(len(name_tokens), len(target_tokens))
        if score > best_score and score >= 0.5:
            best_score = score
            best_target = target

    return best_target


# ============================================================
# 6. POST-PROCESSING
# ============================================================

def remove_parent_child_overlap(df):
    """Remove word overlap between adjacent levels, but only when overlap is significant."""
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']

    for idx in range(len(df)):
        for i in range(1, 5):
            parent = df.at[idx, levels[i-1]]
            child = df.at[idx, levels[i]]
            if not parent or not child or pd.isna(parent) or pd.isna(child):
                continue

            parent_tokens = get_tokens(parent)
            child_tokens = get_tokens(child)
            if not parent_tokens or not child_tokens:
                continue

            overlap = parent_tokens & child_tokens
            # Only remove if > 50% of child words are in parent
            overlap_ratio = len(overlap) / len(child_tokens)
            if overlap_ratio >= 0.5 and len(child_tokens - overlap) > 0:
                remaining = [w for w in child.split() if w.lower() not in overlap or w in ('&', '|')]
                if remaining:
                    new_name = ' '.join(remaining)
                    new_name = new_name.strip(' |&')
                    if new_name and len(new_name) > 1:
                        df.at[idx, levels[i]] = new_name

    return df


def cap_subcategory_count(df, max_children=20):
    """Merge excess subcategories into 'Other' groups."""
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']

    for depth in range(1, 5):
        parent_cols = levels[:depth]
        child_col = levels[depth]

        for parent_key, group in df.groupby(parent_cols):
            children = group[child_col].dropna()
            children = children[children != '']
            unique_children = children.unique()

            if len(unique_children) > max_children:
                child_counts = children.value_counts()
                keep = set(child_counts.head(max_children - 1).index)

                if isinstance(parent_key, str):
                    mask = (df[parent_cols[0]] == parent_key)
                else:
                    mask = pd.Series(True, index=df.index)
                    for col, val in zip(parent_cols, parent_key):
                        mask &= (df[col] == val)

                merge_mask = mask & (~df[child_col].isin(keep)) & (df[child_col] != '') & df[child_col].notna()
                df.loc[merge_mask, child_col] = 'Other Subcategories'

    return df


def check_sibling_overlap(df):
    """Check word overlap between sibling categories."""
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']
    issues = []

    for depth in range(1, 5):
        parent_cols = levels[:depth]
        child_col = levels[depth]

        for parent_key, group in df.groupby(parent_cols):
            siblings = group[child_col].dropna()
            siblings = sorted(siblings[siblings != ''].unique())

            for i in range(len(siblings)):
                for j in range(i+1, len(siblings)):
                    overlap = word_overlap_ratio(siblings[i], siblings[j])
                    if overlap > 0.3:
                        issues.append((parent_key, child_col, siblings[i], siblings[j], overlap))

    return issues


def verify_source_distribution(df):
    """Check source distribution across L1 categories."""
    print("\n=== Source Distribution per L1 ===")
    for l1 in sorted(df['unified_level_1'].unique()):
        subset = df[df['unified_level_1'] == l1]
        total = len(subset)
        src_counts = subset['source'].value_counts()
        sources_present = set(src_counts.index)
        missing = {'amazon', 'facebook', 'google'} - sources_present
        src_str = ', '.join(f"{s}:{src_counts.get(s,0)}" for s in ['amazon','facebook','google'])
        warning = f" *** MISSING: {missing}" if missing else ""
        print(f"  {l1} ({total}): {src_str}{warning}")


# ============================================================
# 7. GENERATE OUTPUTS
# ============================================================

def generate_hierarchy(df):
    levels = ['unified_level_1', 'unified_level_2', 'unified_level_3',
              'unified_level_4', 'unified_level_5']
    all_paths = set()
    for _, row in df.iterrows():
        path = []
        for lvl in levels:
            val = row[lvl]
            if pd.notna(val) and val != '':
                path.append(val)
                all_paths.add(tuple(path + [''] * (5 - len(path))))
    result = pd.DataFrame(list(all_paths), columns=levels)
    result = result.sort_values(levels).reset_index(drop=True)
    return result


# ============================================================
# MAIN
# ============================================================

def main():
    print("Loading data...")
    rows = load_data()
    print(f"Loaded {len(rows)} rows (amazon:{sum(1 for r in rows if r['source']=='amazon')}, "
          f"facebook:{sum(1 for r in rows if r['source']=='facebook')}, "
          f"google:{sum(1 for r in rows if r['source']=='google')})")

    print("\nBuilding L2 consolidation rules...")
    l2_rules = build_l2_consolidation()

    print("Assigning unified levels...")
    results = []
    for row in rows:
        unified, depth = assign_unified_levels(row, l2_rules)
        results.append({
            'source': row['source'],
            'category_path': row['category_path'],
            'depth': depth,
            'unified_level_1': unified[0],
            'unified_level_2': unified[1],
            'unified_level_3': unified[2],
            'unified_level_4': unified[3],
            'unified_level_5': unified[4],
        })

    df = pd.DataFrame(results)

    print("Capping subcategory counts...")
    df = cap_subcategory_count(df)

    # Stats
    print(f"\n=== Level 1: {df['unified_level_1'].nunique()} categories ===")
    for l1 in sorted(df['unified_level_1'].unique()):
        count = len(df[df['unified_level_1'] == l1])
        l2_count = df[df['unified_level_1'] == l1]['unified_level_2'].dropna()
        l2_count = l2_count[l2_count != ''].nunique()
        print(f"  {l1}: {count} rows, {l2_count} L2 subcategories")

    verify_source_distribution(df)

    # Check overlap
    print("\n=== Sibling Overlap Issues (>30%) at L2 ===")
    issues = check_sibling_overlap(df)
    l2_issues = [i for i in issues if i[1] == 'unified_level_2']
    if l2_issues:
        for parent, level, sib1, sib2, overlap in l2_issues[:30]:
            print(f"  Under '{parent}': '{sib1}' vs '{sib2}' = {overlap:.1%}")
    else:
        print("  None found!")

    # Save
    os.makedirs('/root/output', exist_ok=True)

    print("\nSaving unified_taxonomy_full.csv...")
    df.to_csv('/root/output/unified_taxonomy_full.csv', index=False)

    print("Generating hierarchy...")
    hier_df = generate_hierarchy(df)
    print(f"Total unique hierarchy paths: {len(hier_df)}")
    hier_df.to_csv('/root/output/unified_taxonomy_hierarchy.csv', index=False)

    print("\nDone!")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
